add.text: The first terrane collisions on the western edge of North America came in the early Triassic, when the Quesnel, Cache Creek and Stikine terranes combined to form the Intermontane Superterrane.
The likely order of arrival was Yukon-Tanana, Quesnel, Cache Creek and Stikine, although it is also possible these terranes were assembled as one unit before reaching North America.

jura-086.note: first fact dates the Intermontane collisions earlier than the HAVE; kept as sourced

add.text: Distinctive characteristics of carnosaurs include large eye sockets, a long narrow skull, and a thigh bone (femur) longer than the shin (tibia).
The largest carnosaurs can reach up to 10 meters in length.
Most former carnosaurs, such as the megalosaurids, the spinosaurids and the ceratosaurs, were reclassified as more primitive theropods.
There is a paucity of dinosaur fossils from the Early and Middle Jurassic, but by the Late Jurassic dinosaurs were dominating the planet.
The earliest members of the Tetanurae appeared during the late Early Jurassic or early Middle Jurassic.
In the Late Triassic and Early Jurassic there were two stages of rifting, with extension and subsidence, on the western margin of Iberia.
In the Late Jurassic Africa started moving east and the Alpine Tethys opened.

The earliest proposed placental mammal, Juramaia, is Jurassic, yet the earliest known monotreme, Teinolophus, is Cretaceous, even though placentals are more derived and should appear after monotremes.
Recalibrations of genetic and morphological diversity rates have suggested a Late Cretaceous origin for placentals and a Paleocene origin for most modern clades.
Cimmeria, a piece of shelf, traveled north over about 60 million years, pushing the floor of the Paleo-Tethys Ocean under the eastern end of northern Pangaea.
The Neo-Tethys Ocean formed between Cimmeria and Gondwana, directly over where the Paleo-Tethys had been.
As the Atlantic and Arctic oceans opened during the Mesozoic and into the Cenozoic, the Arctic Region went through several stages of rifting, sedimentation and magmatism.
The flood basalts in the Canadian Arctic Islands are similar to the Columbia River flood basalts of the Pacific Northwest.
The first evidence of human fishing is also noted, from artifacts at places such as Blombos Cave in South Africa.
In Africa, bone artifacts and the first art appear in the archaeological record.
Australian megafauna extinction appears to have peaked around 42,000 years ago, earlier than in the Americas or among the Eurasian mammoth steppe fauna.
The giant kangaroo Protemnodon appears to have died out sooner on the Australian mainland than on Tasmania, which humans colonised a few thousand years later.
The Persian Gulf is a foreland basin between the Arabian Peninsula and the Zagros Mountains of Iran.
The retreating ice sheet left meltwater lakes (Lake Algonquin, Lake Chicago, Glacial Lake Iroquois and the Champlain Sea) that filled the basins the glaciers had carved, creating the Great Lakes.
The foundations of the present upper Great Lakes were laid 1.1 to 1.2 billion years ago, when two previously fused tectonic plates split apart and created the Midcontinent Rift.
After the continental ground sloths disappeared, the Caribbean sloths survived about 6,000 years longer, matching the fact that those islands were not colonized by humans until about 5500 yr BP.
Ground sloths ranged from under 100 kilograms in the Caribbean to 3,700–4,100 kilograms in the largest genera Megatherium, Lestodon and Eremotherium.
